coordinate_convention: WGS84 (EPSG:4326) latitude and east-positive longitude in -180..180.
footprint_definition: Square footprint of half-width 0.25 degrees (about 28 km N-S) centred on the site. Smaller than the Mars footprint because Earth analog field sites are typically a few tens of km across; terrain statistics are computed on a grid block-averaged to the MOLA 16 ppd cell size (~3.7 km) so they are comparable to the Mars values.

candidates.name: Atacama Desert - Yungay region
candidates.description: Hyperarid core of the Atacama, with soils so low in organics and microbial life that they were proposed as the closest terrestrial match to Viking-era Mars soil results. Used by NASA ARADS for rover and drill testing.
known_analog_use: NASA ARADS rover and drilling campaigns

candidates.name: McMurdo Dry Valleys - University Valley
candidates.description: Cold, hyperarid polar desert with ice-cemented permafrost and sublimation-dominated landscapes; a long-standing analog for Martian periglacial terrain and the Phoenix landing region.

candidates.name: Haughton impact structure
candidates.description: A 23 km diameter, 39 Myr old impact crater in a polar desert, with impact breccia and hydrothermal mineral deposits. Host to the Haughton-Mars Project field station since 1997.
known_analog_use: Haughton-Mars Project (NASA Ames / Mars Institute / SETI)

candidates.name: Death Valley - central basin
candidates.description: Arid basin-and-range valley with playas, evaporite deposits, alluvial fans and volcanic features, named in the challenge statement as an established Mars analog.
known_analog_use: Named in the Space Apps challenge statement

candidates.name: Holuhraun lava field
candidates.description: Fresh basaltic lava field from the 2014-2015 fissure eruption, surrounded by glacial outwash plains; a close morphological and compositional analog for young Martian volcanic plains.
known_analog_use: ESA / university Mars volcanism analog studies

candidates.name: San Rafael Swell - MDRS area
candidates.description: Semi-arid badlands of Jurassic and Cretaceous sandstone, shale and clays near Hanksville, where the Mars Desert Research Station hosts crewed simulations.
known_analog_use: Mars Desert Research Station crewed simulations

candidates.name: Mauna Kea volcano (summit-centred footprint)
candidates.description: Shield volcano whose upper slopes (tephra cones and basalt above ~3,500 m) are used for ISRU, regolith-excavation and rover trials because of their low vegetation and basaltic soils. NOTE: the 0.5 deg footprint centred on the summit spans the whole upper mountain, so footprint statistics describe the summit region as a whole, not only the test sites.
